items.titleZh: 汉密尔顿与劳森巴库险情暴露2026规则隐患
items.summaryZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿在阿塞拜疆大奖赛二练中因阻碍小红牛车手利亚姆·劳森被FIA干事警告，此事件暴露了2026年新规则在巴库赛道的一大危险。
items.originalTitle: The Baku problem exposed by scary Hamilton and Lawson near-miss
items.summaryEn: Lewis Hamilton received a reprimand for impeding Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson during second practice at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, an incident that exposed one of the major dangers of Formula 1's 2026 rules at the Baku track.
detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿在阿塞拜疆大奖赛第二次练习赛中因阻挡利亚姆·劳森而被罚，这一事件暴露了2026年一级方程式规则在巴库赛道的一大隐患。
国际汽联干事认定，这位法拉利车手在巴库通过18/19号高速弯时挡住了小红牛对手的路线，属于“严重”阻挡。
劳森不得不在时速300公里（186英里）时刹车避让慢悠悠行驶的汉密尔顿。这位新西兰车手随即通过车队电台表达了自己的震惊。
“我的天哪。这真是太危险了，”劳森在事件被认定严重到需要干事介入之前如此说道。
不过，这种情况并不寻常，因为它并不是由练习赛中经常出现的、对更快车辆疏于留意所引发的。
相反，它围绕着本赛季前车队和车手就已经意识到的一个根本性风险点，即受能源限制的2026年赛车以及巴库的赛道布局。
法拉利与小红牛之间的速度差，并不是因为其中一辆全速行驶而另一辆松开油门慢速巡航。在那一刻，两辆车都是全油门。
然而，汉密尔顿的车速只有250公里/小时，而劳森达到了300公里/小时，这是因为他的动力单元处于一种被称为“自动K模式”（auto-k）的模式，在这种模式下电池不进行能量输出，他只依靠内燃机行驶。
这种情况发生在赛道的这一区域，是因为车队不想在计时线之前浪费任何不必要的电池能量。
相反，在19号弯之后的直道上有一个设定的点位，电机发电机组会在那里启动，提供动力提升，以便在单圈开始时获得最大功率和完美的最高速度。
车队和车手在抵达巴库之前就知道，出弯圈上不提早使用电池的赛车与全力释放电能推进的赛车之间会存在速度差。
这就是为什么国际汽联一级方程式比赛总监鲁伊·马克斯在周四上午发布了修订后的赛事说明，试图避免速度不匹配在18/19号弯序列中引发碰撞风险的情况。
马克斯要求处于出场圈或慢速圈的车手从16号弯出口到18号弯之间尽量靠最左侧行驶，然后管理好与后方赛车的差距，以避免在弯道中间被追上而陷入风险。
理论上这个想法不错，但在实践中却难以执行，因为各车队要摸清需要留出多大的差距，本身就很不容易。
汉密尔顿认为自己和法拉利给劳森留出的缓冲距离已经足够，但事实证明他们错了。
"基本上我当时领先四秒，进入最后一个弯时正在推进，"他解释道。"我能看到他。我以为差距够了。我全油门前进。然后就在我们进入18号弯的时候，赛车就像突然没力了一样，他一下子大幅缩短了差距。这种事谁都可能遇上。"
劳森对汉密尔顿所处的境遇表示同情，因为他认为要求车手在18号弯前减速以避免麻烦的做法可能更加危险。
"如果你在18号弯前减速让一辆车过去，那如果你只让那一个人过去还没问题，"他说。"但如果后面还有别人正在推进，比如我当时的情况，你会开到100公里/小时，而我差不多要开到300公里/小时。"
"如果你是前面那辆车，你一给油却发现什么都没有（指抓地力或动力不足），那是一种非常可怕的感觉，因为你甚至来不及让开。"
在干事们调查这起事件的听证会上，他们指出汉密尔顿在16号弯到18号弯之间的直道上没有离开行车线。虽然他们认为汉密尔顿并没有阻挡劳森的意图，但当时的情况非常"严重"，因此应该受到比警告更重的处罚。
但由于两位车手都提到在该区域的能量管理难题已被纳入考量，汉密尔顿只受到了一次警告，而没有受到更严重的处罚。
不过，汉密尔顿认为，国际汽联应该为车队和车手提供更明确的指导方针，说明快速接近的赛车之间需要保持多大差距——他表示打算在周四晚上的车手简报中提出这个问题。
“当你来到一个比赛周末时，没有任何数据或模拟来告诉你：好的，当你来到最后一个弯道并全油门出发，而你的功率比身后正在飞驰圈的车少了500马力时，你需要留出多大的差距才不会被他们追上，”他说。
“所以我认为，需要他们（国际汽联）给出更清晰的指导方针，因为我们这些车手谁都不想惹上麻烦。”
汉密尔顿认为一个更好的办法，他已经告知了干事，就是应当强制要求在18/19号弯全功率输出，以防止赛车之间存在过大的速度差。
“我跟他们说，他们应该做的是在单圈计时、也就是我们做飞驰圈的时候，在最后一个弯用最大功率，”他说。
“然后，当你通过19号弯之后，功率会重置，在这个区域你会多一点功率。应该让任何人都永远不要在18/19号弯慢速行驶。”
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton's reprimand for impeding Liam Lawson during second practice at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix has exposed one of the big dangers with Formula 1's 2026 rules around the Baku track.
The Ferrari driver was deemed by the FIA stewards to have been guilty of "severe" impeding as he got in the way of his Racing Bulls rival through the high-speed Turn 18/19 sweeps in Baku.
Lawson had to hit the brakes and take avoiding action at 300km/h (186mph) to avoid the dawdling Hamilton. The New Zealander expressed his shock about things on the team radio straight after.
"Oh my God. That is so f**king dangerous," declared Lawson, prior to the incident being deemed serious enough to warrant the stewards' intervention later.
The situation is an unusual one though, because it was triggered not by the normal inattention to faster cars that happens frequently in practice.
Instead, it revolved around a fundamental risk point that teams and drivers were aware of ahead of this weekend thanks to the energy starved 2026 cars and the Baku layout.
The speed differential between the Ferrari and Racing Bulls was not because one of them was going flat out and the other was cruising around off the throttle. Both were flat out at that point.

However, Hamilton was only going 250km/h against Lawson's 300km/h because his power unit was in a mode known as 'auto-k', where the battery is not being deployed and he is only running on the internal combustion engine.
That happens in this area of the track because teams do not want to waste any more battery energy than is necessary before the timing line.
Instead, there is a set point on the straight after Turn 19 where the MGU-K will kick in and deliver the power boost for maximum power and perfect top speed when the lap starts.
Teams and drivers knew before they arrived in Baku that the speed offsets between cars on out-laps – so not using battery early – and those pushing on maximum deployment would exist.
That is why F1 race director Rui Marques on Thursday morning issued revised event notes to try to avoid a situation where the speed mismatch risked a collision through the Turn 18/19 sequence.

Marques had demanded that drivers on out or slow laps should keep to the extreme left from the exit of Turn 16 to Turn 18, and then manage the gaps to cars behind to avoid the risk of being caught in the middle of the turns.
In theory the idea was good, but in practice it proved hard to act upon as teams faced an uphill battle in learning the kind of gaps needed.
Hamilton thought that the buffer he and Ferrari had left Lawson was enough, but they were proved wrong.

"I was four seconds ahead basically and I went into the last corner pushing," he explained. "I could see him. I thought the gap was enough. I got into full throttle. And then literally, as we got into [Turn] 18, it's like the car just died, and he swamped up the gap massively. That could happen to anyone."
Lawson had some sympathy with the situation Hamilton had found himself in, as he reckoned that expecting drivers to back off before Turn 18 to avoid trouble was potentially even more dangerous.

"If you slow down before Turn 18 to let a car go, that's fine if you let that guy go," he said. "But if there is somebody else pushing behind like in my situation, you are going to be doing 100km/h and I'm going to be doing nearly 300km/h.
"If you're that car in front and you get on power and you have nothing, it's a really scary feeling because you can't even get out of the way."

During the stewards' hearing to investigate the incident, they noted that Hamilton had not kept off-line on the run between Turns 16 and 18. And while they felt that there had been no intent by Hamilton to block Lawson the situation had been "severe" so deserved something greater than a warning.
But because the energy management headaches in that area that both drivers raised were taken into account, Hamilton was given a reprimand rather than anything more serious.

Hamilton reckoned, however, that teams and drivers should be given better guidelines by the FIA about gaps needed to fast cars approaching – something he said he planned to bring up in Thursday night's drivers' briefing.

"When you come into the weekend, there's no data or simulations to say, OK, when you come to the last corner and you go to full throttle and you have 500bhp less than the car behind you on the lap, this is the gap you need to have before they get on you," he said.
"So I think it's having clearer guidelines from them [the FIA], because none of us drivers want to get in trouble."
Hamilton reckoned a better solution, which he had told the stewards, was that they should mandate maximum deployment through Turns 18/19, to prevent there being big speed differentials between cars.
"I said to them what they should do is on a single lap, when we're doing a push lap, we get max power out of the last corner," he said.
"Then, when you come through [Turn 19], it resets, and you have a little bit more power in here. There should just be nobody going slow ever through [Turns] 18/19."
keyPointsZh: 干事认定汉密尔顿构成"严重"阻碍，事发于巴库高速的18/19号弯路段。
劳森在300公里时速下被迫刹车躲避，并在车队电台直呼极其危险。
当时两车均在全油门行驶，汉密尔顿车速仅为250公里时速，因为其动力单元处于"自动k"模式，电池不输出动力，仅靠内燃机驱动。
keyPointsEn: The stewards deemed Hamilton guilty of "severe" impeding through Baku's high-speed Turn 18/19 section.
Lawson had to brake and take avoiding action at 300km/h and voiced his shock on team radio immediately after.
Both cars were flat out, but Hamilton was only doing 250km/h because his power unit was in 'auto-k' mode, running on the internal combustion engine only without battery deployment.

detailZh: 大卫·库特哈德警告：威廉姆斯FW48升级若失败将有人担责
大卫·库特哈德警告，如果威廉姆斯重大的FW48升级套件未能带来提升，车队可能面临严重后果。
前F1车手大卫·库特哈德警告，如果威廉姆斯升级后的FW48未能立即在性能上取得进步，将会“有人掉脑袋”。
这支格罗夫车队整个赛季都受困于超重赛车。14站过后，它以11分位列车队积分榜第九：卡洛斯·塞恩斯贡献6分，亚历山大·阿尔本贡献5分。
但在本周末的阿塞拜疆大奖赛上，车队现已引入一套重大升级套件，车队领队詹姆斯·沃尔斯称其几乎相当于打造了一辆B版赛车，以期推动车队在发车格上攀升。
在Up To Speed播客的一期节目中，这位前迈凯伦车手解释说，他预计这支由沃尔斯领导的车队会取得可观的跃升。
“我相信，在与车队一些成员交流后，就赛车现在将达到重量标准而言，这是重要的一步，我们知道10公斤约合每圈0.3到0.4秒，”库特哈德说。
“所以带着多余重量参赛只会让自己处于劣势。而它还将朝着他们为明年那辆赛车所采取的方向迈出一步。
“明年的规则有一些空气动力学调整，尤其是底板前部周围，这可能对某些车队有利，也可能对另一些不利。
“但我预计会有点像我们在阿斯顿[马丁]身上看到的那样，他们推出B版赛车后性能有了显著提升。如果这没有发生，当然就会有人掉脑袋，不是吗？”
塞恩斯和阿尔本在巴库的第一节练习赛中分别获得第12和第13名，在第二节练习赛中分别获得第17和第16名。
阿塞拜疆大奖赛将于当地时间周六下午3点（英国时间中午）举行。
detailEn: David Coulthard warns "heads will roll" if Williams FW48 upgrade fails
David Coulthard has warned that Williams could face major consequences if its significant FW48 upgrade package fails to deliver
Former Formula 1 driver David Coulthard has warned that "heads will roll" if Williams's upgraded FW48 fails to deliver an immediate step forward in performance.

The Grove outfit has struggled all season with an overweight car. After 14 rounds, it sits ninth in the constructors' championship with 11 points: six points from Carlos Sainz and five points from Alex Albon.

But it has now introduced a major upgrade package, which team principal James Vowles described as creating an almost B-spec car, at this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix in a bid to propel it up the grid.
During an episode of the Up To Speed podcast, the former McLaren driver explained he expects a decent leap from the Vowles-led team.

"I believe, having spoken to some members of the team, that it is a significant step in terms of the car will now be on weight, which we know 10kg is worth three to four tenths of a second around a lap," Coulthard said.
"So carrying weight is just putting yourself on the back foot. And what it will also do is it will be a step towards the direction they're taking that car for next year.
"There are a few aerodynamic tweaks for next year's regulations, especially around the front of the floor, which may or may not help some teams over others.

"But I'm expecting a little bit like we saw with Aston [Martin], there was a notable step forward in their performance when they brought their B-spec car. And if it doesn't happen, of course there's going to be some heads rolling, isn't there?"
Sainz and Albon finished the first practice session in Baku in 12th and 13th and the second practice session in 17th and 16th, respectively.
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix will take place on Saturday at 3pm local time (noon UK time).

items.originalTitle: Why Mercedes’ huge Baku practice advantage may not be the real picture
items.summaryEn: Mercedes dominated Thursday's practice sessions in Baku, with George Russell fastest in both sessions while Max Verstappen was the closest rival at 0.827s adrift, though the team stressed this advantage does not reflect the true picture for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
detailZh: 为什么梅赛德斯在巴库练习赛中的巨大优势可能并非真实情况
梅赛德斯强调，车队在周四练习赛中展现的巨大优势并不能真实反映F1阿塞拜疆大奖赛的实际局面。然而，几家对手车队却对此留下了深刻印象
梅赛德斯在周四于巴库城市赛道举行的练习赛上发出了非常强有力的宣言。乔治·拉塞尔在两节练习赛中均名列计时榜首位，当天结束时距离他最近的非梅赛德斯赛车落后接近一秒（马克斯·维斯塔潘落后0.827秒）。
梅赛德斯将于在马来西亚站为W17推出期待已久的升级套件，但即使车上没有新部件，拉塞尔的速度也给对手们留下了深刻印象。
红牛本周可以为小红牛22装上最后一份重大升级包，但技术总监皮埃尔·瓦谢承认，他没有预料到与梅赛德斯厂队之间会有如此大的差距。
“是的，我没料到会有这么大的差距，主要是在直道上。之后我们得分析一下这是不是来自尾流（tow）[或者其他原因]。但没错，要达到他们所取得的水平，我们还有工作要做”，当Motorsport.com问及这一差距时，瓦谢这样说道。
“我希望差距能更小一些，但看起来他们比我们快很多。我们会看看能做些什么让赛车更快，但如果这才是真实的差距，那对我们来说将会非常艰难。”
伊萨克·哈贾尔在重返驾驶舱后感觉身体状态完全没问题，但他担心梅赛德斯在周五和周六会真的让红牛望尘莫及。
“有一点吧，[而且也在想]他们为什么能领先这么多。我觉得这非常了不起。我认为我们有一辆不错的车，我们一直和迈凯伦以及法拉利处在同一集团里，但是没错，梅赛德斯，他们已经遥不可及了。”
不过，梅赛德斯自己还没有完全确信自己比其他所有人都高出一个级别。副领队布拉德利·洛德在本周末托托·沃尔夫缺席期间负责车队的运作，他强调车队绝对不应该高兴得太早。
“说实话，我不认为这个差距是有代表性的。我们在第二次自由练习中用软胎跑了更多带有计时的单圈。维斯塔潘只跑了一次，迈凯伦的车手们也一样。”
“可能不要对此过度解读，因为你每跑一个计时的单圈，圈速都在不断提升。我们比别人多跑了一圈，因此可能在赛道上和轮胎上挖掘出的潜力都比他们能找到的要多一些。”
话虽如此，拉塞尔在整天的练习中都显得相当有统治力。这位英国车手在马德里赛后总结称，他已经不再争夺总冠军，只能为分站冠军而战，但巴库比赛周的开始证明非常有希望。
“乔治去年在这里病得很厉害，但仍然拿到第二名。所以这条赛道……我的意思是，他在每条赛道表现都不错，但这是一条他传统上就有非常出色成绩的赛道”，洛德说。
“而且这正是作为一支车队你所希望看到的：如果一辆车遇到麻烦，另一辆就正好在前面领跑。他今天做到了，希望周末剩下的时间里能继续保持这种状态。”
当洛德提到“一辆车遇到麻烦”时，这些话自然是指基米·安东内利。这位积分榜领跑者在第一节练习赛中遭遇液压系统故障，损失了赛道时间——在街道赛道上，这一因素比平时更为重要。
勋爵继续说道：“显然，这让他稍微落后于节奏了，所以他只是缺少圈数、缺少在赛道上的时间，但同样，机械师们干得非常出色。我记得赛车是在一练结束后大约15分钟回来的，而在二练红旗出现的时候，车已经准备好可以出发了。所以他们完成了一项了不起的工作，换掉了引擎，把旧引擎拆出来，把新引擎装进去。
“不会受罚，因为这是备用池里已经有的引擎，而且我们当时已经准备好了。所以我们至少尽可能地挽回了一些练习时间。”
最终的结果是两辆梅赛德斯赛车占据了前两位，并且领先其他车手很大的差距。这给对手们留下了深刻印象，不过法拉利车队领队弗雷德里克·瓦塞尔淡化了周四这些成绩的意义：“我年纪太大了，没精力太关注周五的表现！”
当有人指出现在实际上还是周四时，瓦塞尔笑着总结道：“周五都没什么用，更别提周四了！”
detailEn: Why Mercedes’ huge Baku practice advantage may not be the real picture

Mercedes stresses that its enormous advantage during Thursday’s practice sessions does not show the true picture for the F1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Several rivals, however, have been left highly impressed

Mercedes made a very strong statement during Thursday’s practice sessions at the Baku City Circuit. George Russell topped the times in both sessions, with the first non-Mercedes car almost a second adrift at the end of the day (Max Verstappen at 0.827s).
Mercedes will introduce its long-awaited upgrade package for the W17 in Malaysia, but even without new parts on the car, rivals have been highly impressed by Russell’s pace.
Red Bull can count on the final major upgrade package for the RB22 this week, but technical director Pierre Waché admits he had not expected such a large deficit to the Mercedes works team.

“Yes, I didn't expect this big gap, mainly on the straights. Afterwards we have to analyse if it's coming from a tow [or something else]. But yes, we have work to do to achieve what they have achieved”, Waché said when asked about the gap by Motorsport.com.
“I hope that it's closer, but it looks like they are a lot quicker than us. We will see what we can do to make the car quicker, but if this is the real delta, then it will be tough for us.”
Isack Hadjar, who felt completely fine physically on his return behind the wheel, fears that Mercedes will genuinely be out of Red Bull’s reach on Friday and Saturday.

“A bit, [and thinking] why they are so far away. I think that's very impressive. I think we have a good car, we've been in the mix with McLaren and Ferrari, but yeah, Mercedes, they are out of touch.”

Mercedes itself, however, is not yet fully convinced that it is a class above everyone else. Deputy team principal Bradley Lord, who is taking charge this weekend in Toto Wolff’s absence, stresses that his team absolutely should not celebrate too soon.
“I don't think it's a representative gap, honestly. We ran more timed laps on the soft tyre in FP2. Max only had one go, so did the McLarens.

“Probably don't read too much into it, because every timed lap you did, the lap times were improving. We did one more than everyone else, and therefore probably found a bit more in the track and a bit more in the tyre than they were able to.”

That said, Russell did look commanding throughout the entire day of practice. The Briton concluded in Madrid that he is no longer in the title fight and can only fight for race wins, but the start of the Baku race weekend has proved very promising.

“George was pretty sick here last year and still finished P2. So it's a circuit… I mean, he goes well at every circuit, but this is one where traditionally he's had some really strong results”, Lord said.

“And that's what you're looking for as a team, that if one car hits trouble, the other one's right up there and leading the way. He's done that today and hopefully can continue doing that through the rest of the weekend.”

When Lord mentions that “one car hits trouble”, those words logically refer to Kimi Antonelli. The championship leader suffered a hydraulic problem during the first practice session, costing him track time – a factor that is even more important than usual on a street circuit.

“Obviously it's put him behind the curve a little bit, so he's just missing laps and missing time out on track, but equally, it was a mega job from the mechanics”, Lord continued. “The car came back, I think, 15 minutes after practice, and it was ready to go just as the red flag came out in FP2. So they did an epic job to swap the engine, get the old one out and the new one in.
“No penalty, because it's one that's already in the pool, and yeah, we were ready to go. So we’ve at least salvaged as much of the session as we could.”

The end result is two Mercedes cars at the top with a large gap to the rest. That has impressed the competition, although Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur played down the significance of Thursday’s times: “I’m getting too old to pay too much attention to Friday!”
When it is pointed out that it is actually still Thursday, Vasseur concludes with a laugh: “Friday is useless, imagine the Thursday!”

items.originalTitle: 'The package is delivering as expected' – Audi reflect on new upgrade package after practice ahead of 2026 Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix
items.summaryEn: Audi brought 14 aerodynamic upgrade components to Baku ahead of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with Team Principal Mattia Binotto saying the first impression from the data is that the package is delivering as expected. Only Gabriel Bortoleto ran the new package in FP1, and the two cars finished P14 and P15 in FP2.
detailZh: “套件正按预期交付”——奥迪在阿塞拜疆站练习后谈新升级套件。奥迪为争取本赛季进一步提升性能，在巴库带来了14个新部件。
奥迪领队马蒂亚·比诺托认为，车队在阿塞拜疆大奖赛前引入的重大升级套件“正按预期交付”。
这支欣维尔车队在FIA周末前提交的气动升级清单上勾选了14个类别，其中包括大幅改动的前翼和后翼、修订版地板以及新的引擎盖布局等。
作为相关性验证流程的一部分，一练中只有加布里埃尔·博尔托莱托使用了升级件，从而可以在巴库与尼科·霍肯伯格驾驶的旧规格赛车进行直接对比。
“如果看数据的第一印象，可以说，这套件正按预期交付，”比诺托说。
“这是好事，事实上这也是我们本周末的主要关注点。对我们来说，升级当然对性能很重要，对我们在锦标赛中的竞争也很重要。
“但同样，对我们来说，更重要的是确保车队在方法论和能力方面持续发展。
奥迪在巴库带来大量升级。“因此，从心态上的勇敢，到我们可能交付的气动概念类型，再到交期、工程、生产、制造，我们把挑战提上去了。
“就我们在这里带来的升级而言，最终能带来多少圈速提升并不重要。
“我认为对我们最重要的是，我们提高了挑战，再次在心态和交期等方面推动了整个系统，并希望我们能与风洞和模拟器保持正确的相关性。”
奥迪目前位列车队积分榜第八，仅落后哈斯4分，霍肯伯格和博尔托莱托在最近六场大奖赛中合计五次进入积分区。
博尔托莱托使用新套件在一练中位列第10，紧随其后的是霍肯伯格，随后两人在第二节练习中分列第14和第15。
“我觉得赛车在二练中感觉并不好，”博尔托莱托说。
“说实话，我们缺一点抓地力，还不明白原因。我对此没有答案。
“我猜这就是巴库，低附着、灰尘很大。赛道我想已经好几年没清理过了，我们只能这样开，然后尽力而为。”

detailEn: 'The package is delivering as expected' – Audi reflect on new upgrade package after practice in AzerbaijanAudi have brought 14 new components to Baku in a bid to gain further performance this season.
Audi Team Principal Mattia Binotto believes the team's major upgrade package, which has been introduced ahead of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, is "delivering as expected".

The Hinwil outfit ticked 14 category boxes on the FIA’s pre-weekend submission list of aerodynamic upgrades, which includes substantially changed front and rear wings, a revised floor, and a new engine cover arrangement amongst others.
As part of the correlation process, only Gabriel Bortoleto had the updates in FP1, allowing for a direct comparison with Nico Hulkenberg’s older spec car in Baku.
“If you look at the first, let me say, impression of the data, the package is delivering as expected,” said Binotto.
“Which is good, which is our main focus, as a matter of fact, for the weekend. For us, upgrading, yes, it’s important for the performance, it’s important for our fight in the championship.
“But again, for us, what’s more important is to make sure that the team is developing in terms of methodologies and capacity.

Audi have a big raft of upgrades in Baku"So from being brave when it comes to mindset, to the type of aero concepts we may deliver, on the lead times, engineering, production, manufacturing, we raised the challenge.
"With the upgrade we have brought here, it doesn’t matter how much it will deliver in terms of lap time.

"I think what matters for us the most is having raised the challenge, having again pushed the system on whatever is mindset and lead times, and hopefully we’ll have a correlation which is right compared to the wind tunnel and the sim.”
Audi sit eighth in the teams' standings, just four points behind Haas, with Hulkenberg and Bortoleto having finished in the points at five of the last six Grands Prix between them.
Bortoleto was able to finish P10 in FP1 with the new package, just ahead of Hulkenberg, before the pair finished P14 and P15 in the second session.
“I think the car didn't feel amazing in FP2,” said Bortoleto.
“If I'm very honest, we're lacking a little bit of grip, still to understand why. I don't have answers for that.
“I guess that's Baku, low grip, super dusty. The track has not been cleaned, I think, for a few years now, and yeah, just we need to drive with this and then try our best.”

items.summaryEn: F1 is waiting to see how the situation in the Middle East unfolds before deciding whether the 2026 season finale rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi can go ahead as planned, while preparations have begun at Imola as a contingency venue if a switch is needed.
detailZh: 伊莫拉正在进行准备工作，以防F1需要更换赛季收官战的举办地，但目前的意图仍是继续在卡塔尔和阿布扎比举行比赛。
鉴于今年早些时候迫使巴林和沙特阿拉伯大奖赛取消的持续冲突，F1正在观望中东局势如何发展。
7月底，F1首席执行官斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利表示：“如果局势未能在我们相信应该在9月中旬之前以我们认为应该的方式得到解决，我们将做出决定。”
然而，在本周一F1委员会讨论此事后，各车队预计将在10月中旬前得到答复。
由于物流原因，这是局势需要得到解决的时间点——届时即便是海运至卡塔尔，对11月底的比赛来说也已十分紧张。
F1希望按计划举行卡塔尔和阿布扎比两站比赛，目前这些赛事的准备工作仍在继续，预期它们将如期举行。
但锦标赛无法承受在短时间内发生变化，从而在11月21日拉斯维加斯站之后没有收官战备选方案的情况。
这意味着F1已准备好B计划，据信是伊莫拉——相关工作已经开始，以确保这条意大利赛道在需要时能够承办比赛。
如果最终没有更换至伊莫拉，F1将承担这些工作的费用——包括搭建看台——以保证在需要时有一个随时可用的替代方案。
“我相信伊莫拉正在做准备，以防我们不得不这样做，”哈斯车队领队小松礼雄说。
“我认为挑战在于，例如欧洲房车结构之类的东西——所有照看这些的人，他们冬天有工作，所以我们需要找替代人员来做这些。”
奥迪老板马蒂亚·比诺托也淡化了12月在意大利比赛的天气担忧。
他说，虽然冬天可能会有关于“雪地轮胎”的讨论，“但事实上，伊莫拉每年那个时候的平均气温比（F1举办）拉斯维加斯（站时）更高”。
“而10月中旬，希望我们可能会做出正确的决定。”
detailEn: Preparations are being made at Imola in case Formula 1 needs to switch its season finale venue but the intention is to continue with races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.
F1 is waiting to see how events unfold in the Middle East given the ongoing conflict that forced the cancellation of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian GPs earlier this year.
At the end of July F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali said that "if the situation will not be cleared the way that we believe it should be before the middle of September, we will take the decision".
However, after it was discussed in the F1 Commission on Monday this week, teams are expecting to get an answer by mid-October.
This is the point at which the situation needs to be settled for logistical reasons – even sea freight to Qatar by that point will be cutting it fine for a race at the end of November.
F1 wants to hold the Qatar and Abu Dhabi races as planned and currently preparations for those events continue on the expectation they will go ahead.
But the championship cannot afford for this to change at short notice and leave it without a contingency for a finale after the Las Vegas round on November 21.
That means it has readied a Plan B, understood to be Imola - and work has started to ensure the Italian circuit is able to host a race if needed.
F1 will cover the costs of this work – which includes setting up grandstands – if a switch to Imola does not happen, to guarantee there is a ready-to-go alternative it can turn to if required.
"I believe that Imola is getting ready in case we have to do it," said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu.

"I think the challenges are, for instance, things like European motorhome structure, etc – all those people who look after them, they have a winter job, so we need to find alternative people to do that."
Audi boss Mattia Binotto also played down the weather concerns over a December race in Italy.
He said that while there may be talk about "snow tyres" in wintertime "as a matter of fact, the average temperature in Imola in that time of the year is hotter than [when F1 races in] Las Vegas".
"And mid-October, hopefully we may do the right decision."
keyPointsZh: F1首席执行官斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利7月底曾表示，若局势未能在9月中旬前按预期明朗，将做出决定；但在本周一F1委员会讨论后，各车队预计10月中旬前得到答复。
由于物流原因，10月中旬是必须敲定局势的时间点，届时即便是海运至卡塔尔，对11月底的比赛来说也已十分紧张。
哈斯车队领队小松礼雄表示伊莫拉正在为可能承办比赛做准备，挑战包括欧洲房车结构及相关人员安排；奥迪老板马蒂亚·比诺托则淡化了12月在意大利比赛的天气担忧，称伊莫拉同期平均气温比F1举办拉斯维加斯站时更高。

detailZh: 雅克·维伦纽夫指出杰米·查德威克测试威廉姆斯赛车后女性F1车手面临的障碍
雅克·维伦纽夫表示，F1缺少女性很大程度上归因于人才池太小
1997年F1世界冠军雅克·维伦纽夫表示，当前发车格上缺少女性车手根本上是人才基数问题。
维伦纽夫在阿塞拜疆接受天空体育 F1采访时，与三届W系列赛冠军杰米·查德威克同场。查德威克本周成为十多年来首位测试威廉姆斯F1赛车的女性。维伦纽夫指出，人才池太小是女性在赛车运动中面临的主要问题。
“这很难，因为女性不多，或者说尝试的女性不够多，”维伦纽夫说。“人才池很小，所以这让事情非常困难。每1000名男性中，可能只有1名女性在尝试，这就使情况变得复杂。”
查德威克认为另一个问题是F1可用席位不足，但她补充说，自己的测试证明女性在体能上可以驾驶F1赛车，这让她感到鼓舞。
“我们谈论的是F3冠军、F2冠军，他们都在为获得席位而挣扎。不只是女性在为席位挣扎。每个人都在为席位挣扎。”
“对我来说，那次测试真正巩固的一点是，女性能够胜任，未来也将能够胜任。但正如雅克所说，我们只是需要更多女性参与进来，最终我们会看到一位女性F3冠军、一位女性F2冠军，并最终完全凭借实力进入F1发车格。”
“所以，尽管我很想说，‘是的，我轻松就能应付。’但我不会，因为他们的竞技水平太高了。但就身体上驾驶赛车并坐进座舱而言，这对我的颈部非常艰难，但并非不可能。所以，这是积极的。”
这位28岁的英国车手是威廉姆斯车队大使，在波尔蒂芒赛道驾驶该车队2025款FW47赛车完成了32圈。
detailEn: Jacques Villeneuve identifies barrier facing female F1 drivers after Jamie Chadwick Williams test
Jacques Villeneuve says the lack of women in Formula 1 is largely down to the small talent pool
1997 Formula 1 champion Jacques Villeneuve says the lack of female drivers on the current grid is fundamentally a numbers game.

Speaking on Sky Sports F1 in Azerbaijan alongside three-time W Series champion Jamie Chadwick, who became the first woman in over a decade to test a Williams F1 car this week, Villeneuve pointed to the small talent pool as a major issue for women in motorsport.

"It's tough because there aren't many women, or enough women trying," Villeneuve said. "The talent pool is small, so that makes it very difficult. For 1000 men, maybe you have one woman trying, and then that complicates matters."
Chadwick argued that another issue is the lack of available seats in F1, but added that she was encouraged that her test proved it was physically possible for a woman to race in the machinery.
"We were talking about Formula 3 champions, Formula 2 champions, all struggling to get seats. It's not just women who are struggling to get seats. Everyone is struggling to get seats.

"For me, what doing that test has really solidified is that women can be capable and will be capable in the future. But, as Jacques said as well, we just need more getting into it, and eventually, we're going to see a female Formula 3 champion, a female Formula 2 champion, and ultimately, on [the F1] grid fully on merit.

"So as much as I would have loved to have said, 'Yeah, I'd easily be fine.' I wouldn't, just because of the level that they operate at. But to physically drive the car and get in, it was very tough on my neck, but possible. So, that's positive."
The 28-year-old British driver, who serves as a Williams ambassador, completed 32 laps of the Portimao circuit in the Grove outfit's 2025 FW47 machinery.
